headline: Verano, Curaleaf, Trulieve open Florida stores before Green Wednesday
dek: Verano reaches 89 Florida stores, Curaleaf enters Sebring for its 81st and Trulieve adds Tampa ahead of Green Wednesday on 25 November.
key_points: Verano opens MÜV Tarpon Springs on 20 November, its 89th Florida dispensary and 166th nationwide, and its third new Florida store this month.
Curaleaf opened its first Sebring store on 18 November, bringing it to 81 Florida locations out of 191 nationwide.
Trulieve holds a grand opening for a new Tampa dispensary on 20 November; state data last week showed it running 171 Florida locations.
By our count, Florida is 54% of Verano's store base and 42% of Curaleaf's, making the medical-only state the core of both companies' retail.
body: Three of the largest multistate operators are adding Florida stores in the same week, timed for the busiest shopping stretch of the cannabis year. Verano Holdings said on 19 November it will open MÜV Tarpon Springs on 20 November, its 89th Florida dispensary. Curaleaf opened its first store in Sebring on 18 November, its 81st in the state. Trulieve said it will hold a grand opening at a new Tampa location on 20 November.

All three openings come with launch discounts and land days before Green Wednesday, the day before Thanksgiving, which falls on 25 November this year and which retailers treat as one of their biggest sales days. In a medical-only market where patients must hold a state card, new doors are one of the few levers operators have to win share.
## Verano: third new store this month

Verano said MÜV Tarpon Springs is its sixth location in Pinellas County and its third MÜV opening this month, raising its national count to 166 dispensaries. Its 88th Florida store, in Daytona Beach, was announced on 12 November. The company is pairing the opening with storewide discounts through Green Wednesday week, including up to 50% off some products, and a ribbon-cutting on 23 November.

By our arithmetic, 89 of Verano's 166 stores, or about 54%, are now in Florida. That concentration makes the state's rules on store caps, product types and federal registration more important to Verano than to almost any other operator.

Curaleaf's Sebring store, at 4226 Sebring Parkway in Highlands County, is in a market the company had not served before. Chairman and CEO Boris Jordan said local patients would no longer have to travel far to shop with the company. A two-day grand opening runs on 20 and 21 November with giveaways for the first patients each day.

The opening takes Curaleaf to 81 Florida locations and 191 nationwide, so Florida is about 42% of its US store count by our arithmetic. As we reported this morning, Curaleaf also kept a federal appeals win this week in a $31.8 million contract case. Florida retail is the steady base under the company's wider ambitions.
> In a medical-only state, a new store is a bet on patient count, not on legalisation.

Trulieve's new store, Trulieve Tampa Hillsborough West at 13829 West Hillsborough Avenue, opens with walk-in and express pickup. The company is offering a 60% discount for first-time customers and 20% off for veterans across Florida. CEO Kim Rivers said the store expands the company's presence in Hillsborough County.

Trulieve is still the clear leader. As we reported on 14 November, the state's weekly figures showed it dispensing about 35% of the week's smokable flower from 171 locations, and active patients across Florida stood at 943,852. Green Dragon's count jumped to 74 locations after Vireo Growth's takeover of FLUENT closed on 9 November.

These openings also come as Florida operators sort out their federal status under Schedule III. As we reported on 12 November, Trulieve said DEA registration ended its Section 280E tax burden. That gives Florida operators a cost advantage that dual-licence operators in states such as Massachusetts, where the regulator says it has no federal guidance, do not yet share.

Registered dispensaries face the same 29 November DEA deadline as everyone else to trade only with registrants or timely applicants. Operators that grow and process their own product, as the big Florida chains do, have fewer outside trading partners to vet than stores that buy from independent growers. That is our assessment.

For investors, the store race shows where the big operators see growth: more doors in a large, stable medical market with federal tax relief, rather than waiting on adult-use votes. The risk is that each new store competes with the others for a patient base of roughly 944,000. Heavy launch discounts, from 50% off at Verano to 60% for Trulieve's new customers, suggest the fight for patients is being paid for partly in margin. That is our assessment.

Watch Florida's weekly patient and dispensing data after Green Wednesday on 25 November for any shift in share, Verano's ribbon-cutting on 23 November, and further openings before year-end. Also watch whether any Florida operator reports problems meeting the DEA's 29 November supply-chain deadline.
